newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE to make adjustments to 90-day bill options.
newsitem.headline: SFE to make adjustments to 90-day bill options.

text.p: The Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) said that from Monday April 7 the 90-day bank bill options contract will be traded and quoted in increments of 0.005 percent rather than 0.01 percent.

SFE chief executive Les Hoskings said the move to trading in "half ticks" followed extensive consultation between the exchange and market participants, and will allow market users to more accurately price and trade "out of the money" options.
"Out of the money options have very small premium values and the move to half tick trading makes it easier for market users to price and trade these contracts," Hosking said.
"It will also allow for more precise end of day settlement prices, thereby ensuring the calculation of more precise variation margins," he added.
He also said that options trading at the SFE rose to an all time high during 1996, with a record 906,000 90-day bank bill options traded.
